_comment: Mutation testing for the reports UI: the page that lists reports, the tab that runs one, the generic list renderer, the form-renderer map, the shared error panel, and the download path (the export transport plus the shared browser-download helpers). Standalone config rather than an addition to an existing one, for the reason stryker.listhooks.config.json was split out: every mutant pays for every test in the run's include list, so unrelated files do not belong in the same run. WHY THESE FILES: the reporting epic's Key Result is that adding a report costs only a template, and on this side that rests on the UI drawing whatever columns, rows and form the API sends. The failure is silent -- a renderer that quietly ignores a column, or a page that keeps showing the previous report's rows after you pick a different one, renders perfectly and shows the wrong answer. Line coverage cannot see either. The download path fails just as quietly: a file saved under the wrong name, or saved from locally-rebuilt rows rather than the server's export, still downloads. MUTATOR SET: StringLiteral disabled, which is DELIBERATELY different from stryker.pilot.config.json -- read the reasoning there before copying either way. In the pilot the string literals ARE the behaviour ('admin.auth' is the permission a hook checks). Here they are Tailwind class lists and user-facing prose; the one string that is behavioural, the 'list' key of FORM_RENDERERS, is asserted directly by formRenderers.test.js. ObjectLiteral stays ENABLED: the renderer map is an object literal and emptying it must be caught. THE FOUR REMAINING SURVIVORS ARE ANALYSED, NOT UNEXAMINED, and are left visible rather than declared away (the floor sits below the measured score, so they cost nothing). Three are the React `key` expression at ListReportRenderer.jsx:35 (`row._entity?.id || i` -> true / false / &&): a key is never rendered into the DOM, so no assertion any test can make distinguishes them; they would only matter as reconciliation bugs across a re-render with reordered rows, which this list does not do (a refresh replaces the whole table). Revisit if the list ever gains sorting or in-place row updates. The fourth is useFetch's `initialData: []` in ReportsPage.jsx: the page returns its loading pane until the request resolves and its error panel if it fails, so no render ever reads the initial value -- it declares the shape of `data`, and only a test asserting on an unreachable state could kill it. Everything else in the run is killed: ReportViewPage.jsx, reportExport.js, download.js and ReportError.jsx are all at 100%. Enforced: see MUTATION FLOOR below. Run: cd app/ui && npm run test:mutation:reports MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score, and is a RATCHET -- it only ever goes up. It is enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml (never on a PR: mutation is far heavier than the unit suite). The margin is not slack to spend, it absorbs the two things that legitimately move a score without anyone editing a test: a Stryker/vitest upgrade that changes which mutants are generated, and timeouts, which count as killed and can flip under CI load. Raise the floor when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green -- a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 97.81% when the floor was set to 96. NOT YET IN THE WEEKLY MATRIX: .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml lists its scopes explicitly, and this one is not in that list yet -- add `{ pkg: ui, name: reports, label: 'UI reports' }` to the matrix so the floor above is actually enforced weekly. Until then the score here is measured and committed but not gated.

mutationExclusions.src/components/reports/ask/SpecEditor.js: A form that draws whatever the API catalog declares — selects for fields, operators and values, plus the add/remove wiring. Its behaviour IS the report definition it produces, and that is asserted where it is enforced: validateSpec / compileSpec on the API side (both mutated), and end-to-end in app/ui/e2e/custom-reports.spec.js, which builds a report by hand and runs it. Mutating the JSX and Tailwind here measures markup.
Conversation shell around POST /api/nl-reports/interpret: it renders turns, polls while the model prepares its prompt cache, and hands a definition to the builder. The decisions it makes are the API contract (report / clarify / confirm), asserted in routes/nlReports.test.js and service.test.js; the model half cannot be exercised in a sandbox without a model server.
mutationExclusions.src/components/reports/ask/ReportBuilder: Page composition: name and description fields, the assistant, the editor, the preview and save/delete. Every behaviour it has is an API call whose contract is mutated API-side, and the whole path is covered end-to-end (new → criteria → preview → save → run → edit → delete).
mutationExclusions.src/components/admin/ReportGeneratorLLMS: Read-only status card in Admin → LLM: the shipped model name, whether the server answers, and a Test button that calls the warm-up endpoint. No state of its own beyond the button; the endpoint it reports on is mutated API-side.
Three Tailwind class strings shared by the assistant's parts, and nothing else. StringLiteral mutations are disabled in this config for exactly this kind of value, so no mutant could be generated here that measures behaviour.

Draws one conversation turn from a reply the API already decided (report / clarify / confirm / error). The decisions it shows are mutated where they are made — useAskConversation.js here, service.js and routes/nlReports.js API-side — and what it renders is asserted by AskAssistant.Turn.mount.test.jsx; mutating its JSX would measure markup.
mutationExclusions.src/components/reports/ask/ReportBuilder: Presentational sections of the report builder: header buttons, name/description fields, the definition panel and the results area. The state they display and the actions they trigger live in useReportPreview.js and useSavedReportActions.js, which are mutated; the page is covered end-to-end in e2e/custom-reports.spec.js and by ReportBuilderParts.mount.test.jsx.
